item.title: Setting Up a Test of a Claimed Mean Clinic Wait
item.stimulus: A clinic posts a sign saying that patients wait a mean of 20 minutes to see a provider. A patient advocate suspects the true mean wait is more than 20 minutes. The advocate takes a random sample of 18 patients from the hundreds seen this month and records each wait. The sample mean is 23.1 minutes and the sample standard deviation is 5.8 minutes. A dotplot of the sample shows no strong skewness and no outliers.

parts.prompt: Define the parameter of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ as the true mean waiting time, in minutes, of all patients seen at this clinic this month.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ as the true mean waiting time, in minutes, of all patients seen at this clinic this month, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ = 20 and Hₐ: μ > 20.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ = 20 and Hₐ: μ > 20, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure and show that its conditions are met.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a one-sample t-test for a population mean.
criteria.evidence: Response names a one-sample t-test for a population mean.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the 18 patients were randomly selected.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the 18 patients were randomly selected.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: 18 patients are less than 10% of the hundreds seen this month.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: 18 patients are less than 10% of the hundreds seen this month.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: n = 18 is less than 30, but the dotplot of the sample shows no strong skewness and no outliers.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition and why it is met: n = 18 is less than 30, but the dotplot of the sample shows no strong skewness and no outliers.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) μ is the true mean waiting time, in minutes, of all patients seen at this clinic this month. H₀: μ = 20 versus Hₐ: μ > 20.

(b) The procedure is a one-sample t-test for a population mean, Randomization: the 18 patients were randomly selected. 10% condition: 18 patients are less than 10% of the hundreds seen this month. Sample-data condition: n = 18 is less than 30, but the dotplot of the sample shows no strong skewness and no outliers.
item.verification_python:
mu0, n = 20, 18
assert n < 30
assert 23.1 > mu0
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
